title: H-shaped sponge positioner prevents pressure injuries during prolonged prone ventilation in acute respiratory distress syndrome: a single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial.
authors: Wang Y, Liu J, Chen S, Tian S, Hu S, Tang B, Zeng L, Luo L
abstract: In patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome, prolonged prone position ventilation is frequently employed to enhance oxygenation but often results in pressure injuries. To protect patients from such injuries, a new H-shaped sponge locator was designed in the study. In this single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial, 60 patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome requiring extended prone position ventilation (≥ 12 hours per session) were recruited from the General Intensive Care Unit at Xiangtan Central Hospital, Hunan Province, China, between May 2023 and May 2024. Participants were randomly allocated to either the intervention group, which received prone positioning with the assistance of the H-shaped sponge positioner, or the control group, which used conventional soft pillows for support. The primary outcomes included the number of anatomical sites affected by pressure injuries and injury severity, classified according to the revised 2016 National Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel/the European Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel staging criteria. Secondary outcomes included mean airway pressure, oxygenation index (PaO2/FiO2), intravesical pressure, and the frequency of support device adjustments. Data from 29 patients in each group were analyzed. Significant group × time interactions were observed for both the number of pressure injury sites and overall incidence. Although pressure injuries increased progressively across all sessions in both groups, patients in the intervention group consistently had fewer injury sites. There were no significant group × time interactions for mean airway pressure or intravesical pressure. However, both measures increased over time in all patients, with significantly lower values in the intervention group. Oxygenation index improved over time, with no statistically significant differences between groups. The intervention group required markedly fewer support device adjustments. In patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome receiving extended prone position ventilation, the H-shaped sponge positioner significantly outperformed standard soft pillow support in preventing pressure injuries. This cost-efficient device not only minimized the number and severity of pressure ulcers but also reduced mean airway and intra-abdominal pressures and decreased the frequency of nursing interventions. Given its ease of use and affordability, the H-shaped positioner holds substantial promise for clinical application, particularly in resource-constrained settings, and warrants further evaluation in broader implementation studies. This trial was registred at National Health Security Information Platform (Medical Research Registration and Information System, https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn, Registration No. MR-43-23-039592) on March 30, 2023.

title: Super-speciality medicine in India: A critical review of growth referral gaps and cluster-based reform.
authors: Ghosh K
abstract: Super-speciality medical education in India has expanded rapidly over the past four decades, increasing from fewer than 100 seats in the 1980s to more than 5000 DM/MCh/DrNB seats by 2025. This growth reflects advances in diagnostics and surgical technology, as well as the rising burden of complex non-communicable diseases. Up to 45-58% of tertiary visits involve conditions manageable at primary levels, while rural regions face severe shortages of super-specialists, with 80-85% of specialists concentrated in urban districts. Private multispeciality hospitals host most high-skilled professionals, reinforcing geographic and sectoral inequities. Training quality also varies widely due to faculty shortages, commercialisation, and inconsistent regulatory enforcement. Emerging disciplines such as genomics, metabolic medicine, and precision medicine remain poorly integrated within siloed DM/MCh structures. This critical narrative review synthesised peer-reviewed literature, regulatory documents and national datasets published between 1980 and 2025, identified through a structured search and analysed using the World Health Organization (WHO) health system building blocks framework. The review argues for restructuring India's medical education and service delivery architecture by strengthening general practice, enforcing referral pathways, and standardising training quality. A cluster-based model linking primary care, secondary hubs, and tertiary precision centres is proposed, with reform pathways organised across all six building blocks, to align super-speciality expertise with population needs. Because the evidence relies heavily on a small number of apex institutions and states and on grey literature, the findings should be interpreted with caution.

title: Next-generation anti-obesity drugs: emerging molecular targets and translational opportunities.
authors: Shetty S, Rangle A, Mukherjee AG, Bharti AK, Jena SP, Prince SE, Gopalakrishnan AV
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
abstract: PURPOSE: Obesity is a heterogeneous, chronic metabolic disease driven by dysregulation of energy homeostasis across interconnected central nervous system, gastrointestinal, adipose, endocrine, immune, and mitochondrial networks. Despite the established roles of lifestyle intervention and metabolic/bariatric surgery, limitations in accessibility, durability, and interindividual response have stimulated the development of mechanism-based pharmacotherapies. This review critically examines emerging therapeutic strategies targeting integrated energy-regulatory pathways and evaluates their translational potential for precision obesity management. METHODS: Current evidence was synthesized across major biological systems governing appetite, energy expenditure, and metabolic adaptation. Central melanocortin, Neuropeptide Y (NPY)/ Agouti-related peptide (AgRP), serotonergic, dopaminergic, and endocannabinoid pathways were considered alongside gut-derived incretin, amylin, Peptide YY (PYY), ghrelin, Fibroblast Growth Factor (FGF), and bile acid signaling. Emerging approaches targeting adipose remodeling, thermogenesis, mitochondrial energetics, AMPK-mTOR-sirtuin signaling, inflammation, and fibrosis were also evaluated. Genetic, epigenetic, and artificial intelligence-based approaches to patient stratification were incorporated to assess prospects for precision therapy. RESULTS: Obesity pharmacotherapy is shifting from conventional appetite suppression toward coordinated modulation of interconnected metabolic pathways. Incretin-based and multi-agonist therapies provide the strongest clinical evidence for substantial weight reduction and metabolic improvement. However, treatment discontinuation, weight regain, adverse effects, cost, and heterogeneous therapeutic responses remain major challenges. Strategies targeting adipose tissue dysfunction, mitochondrial metabolism, thermogenesis, immune-metabolic signaling, and fibrosis offer additional opportunities for disease modification, although many remain in preclinical or early clinical development. Increasing evidence for biological heterogeneity supports individualized therapeutic selection. CONCLUSION: The emerging therapeutic paradigm positions obesity as a systems-level disorder requiring mechanism-informed, individualized intervention. Integrating CNS-gut-adipose-mitochondrial biology with multi-omics, biomarkers, and artificial intelligence may enable more durable and precise treatment. Long-term safety, durability, affordability, equitable access, and clinical validation remain essential for translation.

title: A topologically engineered hydrogel platform targeting IL11 promotes renal repair after partial nephrectomy.
authors: Yu Z, Dong X, Li F, Zhang Y, Dai S, Cao N, Jia X, Zhao J
abstract: Partial nephrectomy (PN) is the gold standard for treating renal tumors and trauma; however, massive nephron loss and persistent fibrosis readily lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Current therapeutic options remain non-curative and costly, as nearly half of PN patients inevitably progress to end-stage renal failure. Here, we present an innovative regenerative platform for PN-induced CKD, integrating structural biomimicry with targeted molecular inhibition. Harnessing light-based bioprinting of gelatin and hyaluronic acid methacrylates coupled with removable alginate microfiber, we constructed a hierarchical channel scaffold (HCS) that features precisely patterned macrochannels and template-derived microchannels, which closely mimics native kidney architecture, provides structural support, and remarkably enhances cell migration (∼5.45-fold) and rapid neovascularization (∼7.66-fold) over unidirectional channel structures. Moreover, interleukin 11 (IL11) was identified as a novel therapeutic target in kidney fibrosis after PN. Thus, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells loaded with IL11 small interfering RNA (siIL11) were homogeneously encapsulated into HCS, achieving over 4-fold higher renal retention than systemic delivery in PN-induced CKD mice. Furthermore, sustained local release of EV-siIL11 and hierarchically channeled HCS guided synergistic regenerative effects that remarkably inhibited fibrosis, cell cycle arrest, and immune responses, thereby potently preventing kidney atrophy and restoring renal structure with newly aligned nephrons and vasculature, ultimately recovering kidney function. Further analysis revealed that IL11 silencing reversed epithelial‒mesenchymal transition by suppressing the STAT3-ERK-GSK3β-SNAI1 axis. This topological multifunctional hydrogel platform offers a localized, sustained, and clinically translatable strategy for postsurgical kidney regeneration.

title: Low-dose carbon monoxide in cardiovascular surgery: mechanisms, monitoring, and therapeutic potential.
authors: Zou J, Wang J, Wang T, Zhang H, Zhang J, Ji B
abstract: Carbon monoxide has been regarded as a toxic gas for a long time, however, recent studies have demonstrated that carbon monoxide, as an endogenous gaseous signaling molecule generated via the heme oxygenase system, plays an important regulatory role in various physiological and pathological processes. Physiologically, endogenous carbon monoxide production is approximately 400-500 μmol per day, whereas freely diffusible carbon monoxide remains very low, at about 0.002 μM, or approximately 2.5 ppm as an equivalent gas-phase concentration. At low concentrations, carbon monoxide exerts diverse biological effects, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, vasoregulatory, mitochondrial-modulating, and anti-remodeling actions. These properties are particularly relevant to cardiovascular surgery, especially procedures involving cardiopulmonary bypass, where systemic inflammation, ischemia-reperfusion injury, hemolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and microcirculatory disturbance contribute substantially to perioperative morbidity. During cardiopulmonary bypass, endogenous carbon monoxide production may increase and can be indirectly assessed by carboxyhemoglobin and exhaled carbon monoxide, suggesting a potential role for carbon monoxide-related measurements as dynamic biomarkers of hemolysis, inflammation, and surgical stress. In parallel, preclinical studies have shown that low-dose inhaled carbon monoxide and carbon monoxide-releasing molecules may alleviate inflammatory responses, preserve mitochondrial function, protect the vascular endothelium, and reduce cardiovascular surgery-related organ injury under controlled experimental conditions. Nevertheless, the translational application of carbon monoxide remains limited by its narrow therapeutic window, dose- and time-dependent biological effects, interindividual variability, and the need for rigorous perioperative monitoring. This review summarizes the sources, metabolism, molecular targets, and cardiovascular effects of carbon monoxide, with a focus on its monitoring value and therapeutic potential in cardiovascular surgery. We further discuss current evidence, safety considerations, and future directions for translating low-dose carbon monoxide and carbon monoxide-releasing strategies into perioperative cardiovascular care.

title: Kidney effects of inhaled nitric oxide in critically ill patients: from pathophysiological considerations to clinical implications.
authors: Robert A, Gonze A, Bulpa P, Hauquiert B
abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide is widely used as a selective pulmonary vasodilator in critical care, yet its renal effects remain controversial. While existing reviews mostly focus on indications for inhaled nitric oxide and its impact on outcomes, limited data exist on its renal effects, since it was thought to act only locally in the lungs. This review examine the clinical evidence regarding kidney outcomes associated with inhaled nitric oxide across major indications and provide an integrated mechanistic analysis of nitric oxide signaling in renal physiology and pathophysiology. Nitric oxide is produced by nitric oxide synthases using L-arginine as a substrate. It acts as a smooth muscle relaxation factor and ultimately causes vasodilation through its effect on cyclic guanosine monophosphate. Nitric oxide plays a pivotal role in renal hemodynamic regulation, glomerular filtration, tubular function, and microcirculatory homeostasis. The net renal effect of inhaled nitric oxide likely reflects the balance between improved nitric oxide signaling and oxidative stress generation. Available clinical data suggest that the renal impact of inhaled nitric oxide is context-dependent. In acute respiratory distress syndrome, higher-level evidence indicates a potential increase in acute kidney injury, possibly related to oxidative and nitrosative stress. Conversely, in cardiac bypass surgery, inhaled nitric oxide may confer nephroprotection by restoring nitric oxide bioavailability during hemolysis and free hemoglobin-mediated nitric oxide scavenging. In other conditions, including organ transplantation, pulmonary hypertension, sepsis, and hemolytic disorders, evidence remains limited or inconclusive. Overall, current evidence does not support a uniform renal effect of inhaled nitric oxide, indicating the need for prospective studies with predefined renal endpoints to clarify its clinical relevance.

title: Critical Care Management of Disaster-Related Organ Failure.
authors: Hertel K, Bard M
journal: The Surgical clinics of North America
abstract: Disasters generate high volumes of multisystem trauma while simultaneously degrading the staff, equipment, and electricity that critical care depends on. This article reviews management of disaster-related organ failure under resource constraint. It outlines step-wise respiratory support, from high-flow nasal cannula and noninvasive ventilation to lung-protective mechanical ventilation; prevention and treatment of acute kidney injury (AKI), including dialysis options for AKI and end-stage renal disease patients; recognition of hemorrhagic, neurogenic, cardiogenic, and obstructive shock; and secondary complications including coagulopathy, hypothermia, abdominal compartment syndrome, hepatic dysfunction, and hyperglycemia. Ethical triage, palliation, telecritical care, and staffing models are also addressed.

title: Gegen qinlian decoction alleviates DSS-induced colitis through modulation of intestinal stem cell homeostasis and M1 macrophage polarization.
authors: Wang M, Yang X, Ji N, Wang X, Cheng Y, Liu Z, Ren L, Leng Z
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) imposes a significant burden on human health and socioeconomic systems. Gegen Qinlian Decoction (GQD) is an effective formula clinically used for the treatment of IBD. However, the underlying mechanisms of GQD in treating colitis remain incompletely elucidated. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of GQD in DSS-induced colitis mice, and explore the underlying mechanisms, thereby providing novel perspectives and strategies for colitis treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A mouse colitis model was induced by administering 2.5% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) in drinking water. The therapeutic efficacy of GQD was assessed by monitoring body weight, disease activity index (DAI), colon length, histopathological damage, inflammatory cytokines, and intestinal mechanical and mucus barrier function. RNA sequencing was performed to reveal the underlying mechanisms. The effects of GQD on macrophage polarization and intestinal stem cells (ISCs) restoration were subsequently examined. RESULTS: GQD treatment significantly alleviated DSS-induced colitis and tissue damage, accompanied by restoration of tight junction protein expression and improvement of mucus barrier function. RNA sequencing suggested that the effects of GQD in colitis mice were closely associated with ISCs and macrophage functions. Experimental validation demonstrated that GQD treatment was associated with increased expression of ISC-associated markers, including AXIN2, and improved goblet cell-associated mucus barrier parameters. Meanwhile, GQD treatment attenuated M1 macrophage polarization, accompanied by decreased inflammatory cytokine levels and alleviation of intestinal inflammation. These effects were also accompanied by reduced SNX10 expression and alterations in Wnt/β-catenin and NLRP3/caspase-1 signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: GQD ameliorates intestinal mucosal barrier function and promotes mucosal healing in DSS-induced colitis mice. These effects are associated with the upregulation of ISC-related markers expression and the inhibition of M1 macrophage polarization.

title: EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework reveals mechanistic insights of Buyang Huanwu Decoction in ischemic stroke with experimental validation.
authors: Qiao R, Liu C, Pan X, Tian Q, He F
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHWD), a classical formula recorded in Yilin Gaicuo, has been widely used for the treatment of stroke and post-stroke sequelae in traditional Chinese medicine. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to establish a novel framework based on the EWMCRITIC-VIKOR algorithm to prioritize potential BYHWD targets against IS by integrating multi-dimensional biological features, with validation through in vivo experiments. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 14 biological features across 4 dimensions were quantified. Feature weights were calculated using EWM and CRITIC, and integrated via VIKOR for MCDM on BYHWD-IS overlapping targets. The therapeutic effects of BYHWD were validated in middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model. Anti-inflammatory effects were assessed by RT-qPCR and ELISA, while western blotting were used to evaluate signaling via the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway. RESULTS: The EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework prioritized 5 key targets (FOS, IL1β, AKT1, TP53, and IL6) from 239 overlapping targets. The VIKOR compromise solution exhibited a distinct low-Q priority set, in which the top targets jointly minimized group utility and individual regret, and the overall ranking showed weak association with logFC, indicating that prioritization was not driven by expression effect size alone. BYHWD treatment significantly improved MCAO-induced brain injury. RT-qPCR and ELISA showed marked downregulation of IL1B and IL6 after BYHWD treatment, and western blotting indicated altered PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling status. CONCLUSION: The EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework enables robust prioritization of therapeutic targets by integrating heterogeneous biological data. This approach enhances mechanistic understanding of BYHWD in IS and offers a reliable strategy for target discovery in herbal interventions.

title: Ulcerative colitis imaging via a ratiometric fluorescent probe with large emission shift for SO2 sensing.
authors: Long S, Gao S, Liu Y, Zhang J, Shi H, Wang A, Zhang Y, Chen W
abstract: Sulfur dioxide (SO2) serves as a gaseous signaling molecule that exerts pivotal regulatory functions in diverse physiological and pathological processes and has emerged as a novel gaseous biomarker associated with multiple inflammatory and hepatic diseases. Ulcerative colitis (UC), a diffuse inflammatory bowel disease primarily affecting the colonic mucosa, manifests as chronic inflammation. However, direct ratiometric visualization of SO2 in UC lesions has remained challenging due to the scarcity of ratiometric fluorescent probes with large emission shifts suitable for in vivo imaging. Herein, we present SL, a ratiometric fluorescent probe that reports SO2 via analyte-induced dual-emission rearrangement with a large spectral shift. Using SL, we captured dynamic SO2 signals at the cellular level and visualized endogenous SO2 changes in UC mice. These findings demonstrate that SL enables the examination of SO2 dynamics in living systems and may facilitate investigations of SO2-associated signaling events in inflammatory pathological contexts.

title: Active components alignment of Gegen Qinlian Decoction for inflammatory bowel disease: exploring the possible role of the SphK1/S1P/NF-κB pathway.
authors: Liu S, Zhang D, Zong Z, Hu Y, Bai J, Li J, Sun W, Yang X
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Gegenqinlian Decoction (GQD) has been used as a folk remedy for gastrointestinal diseases in China over thousands of years, and demonstrates significant efficacy against inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We previously showed that the active components alignment of GQD inhibits nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) p65 signal transduction and plays a key role in preventing and treating IBD. With growing insights into the gut microbiota and its metabolites, the molecular mechanisms underlying therapeutic effects of GQD against IBD require further elucidation. This is particularly relevant given the previously reported relationship between the host NF-κB pathway and the gut microbiota. AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the therapeutic mechanisms of GQD and its aligned active components against IBD, with a focus on microbiota-involved regulation of the host sphingosine kinase 1 (SphK1)/sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P)/NF-κB signaling pathway, using both 2,4,6-Trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced rat colitis and dextran sulfate sodium salt (DSS)-induced mouse colitis models and cultured cells. MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this research, the therapeutic effect of GQD on TNBS-induced colitis rats was evaluated through the measurement of body weight, colorectal length, disease activity index (DAI), colon length and hematoxylin-eosin staining. 16S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted metabolomic analyses were performed to evaluate the restoration of gut microbial and metabolic homeostasis by GQD. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were then utilized to explore the potential relationships between specific targets and the active components alignment (ACA) of GQD on IBD treatment. To further validate the in vivo effects of the ACA, a dextran sulfate sodium salt (DSS)-induced mouse colitis model was established, and body weight, DAI, colorectum length, histopathology, S1P levels, and SphK1/S1PR1 expression were assessed. Experimental validation in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages and NCM460 colonic epithelial cells was subsequently conducted to determine whether this active components alignment suppressed the SphK1/S1P/NF-κB pathway via molecular and cellular assays, including cell metabolomics, ELISA, Western blot, and immunofluorescence staining. RESULTS: GQD significantly relieved symptoms, colonic inflammation, and intestinal damage in TNBS-induced colitis rats. It partially reversed gut microbiota dysbiosis, modulated sphingolipid metabolic pathways, and downregulated the expression of sphingolipid-related Sphk1 and S1PR1 proteins, as well as S1P levels, in colon tissues (p < 0.05). In the DSS-induced mouse colitis model, the ACA of GQD significantly alleviated body weight loss, DAI, colorectum shortening, and histopathological damage, and reduced S1P levels and SphK1/S1PR1 expression in colon tissues (p < 0.05 or p < 0.01). In vitro, the ACA of GQD attenuated LPS-induced inflammatory responses in RAW264.7 macrophages and NCM460 colonic epithelial cells, as reflected by significant reductions in the levels of NO, ROS, and pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β, and S1P production (p < 0.05 or p < 0.01). Mechanistic dissection revealed that this ACA of GQD suppressed SphK1 expression and S1P production, inhibiting IκBα degradation and NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation, as directly evidenced by immunofluorescence staining, thus repressing the transcription of downstream pro-inflammatory genes and alleviating intestinal inflammation. CONCLUSION: GQD restored gut microecological homeostasis and rectified sphingolipid metabolic disturbances. Its active components alignment afforded anti-inflammatory and colitis-protective effects, partially via modulation of the SphK1/S1P/NF-κB signaling pathway. The consistent therapeutic and mechanistic effects observed in both TNBS-induced rat colitis and DSS-induced mouse colitis support that the eight-component alignment largely recapitulates the key effects of the complete GQD formulation. These findings provide novel mechanistic insights and a scientific rationale for the clinical application of GQD in the management of IBD.

title: Association of retinal abnormalities and adverse cardiac events in patients with coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes.
authors: Qian HMK, Konttinen AKE, Holmström LTA, Wirkkala JPK, King ISE, Lepojärvi ES, Tulppo MP, Perkiömäki JS
abstract: BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association of retinal abnormalities and cardiac mortality in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) and type 2 diabetes (DM). METHODS: The ARTEMIS study is a prospective cohort study of 1,946 patients (68% male; mean age 66.9 ± 8.6 years) diagnosed with CAD. Type 2 DM was diagnosed in 834 patients (43%), and 525 (27%) of them had retinal images available. RESULTS: During mean follow-up of 8.7 ± 2.2 years, 54 cardiac deaths occurred. From all analyzed retinal abnormalities, diabetic retinopathy (DR) was associated with cardiac death (p = 0.005). DR was independently associated with increased risk of cardiac death (DR 16.2% vs. non-DR 8.4%; hazard ratio [HR] 2.0, 95% CI: 1.0-4.0, p = 0.04) when adjusted with confounding factors. DR was associated with sudden cardiac death (SCD) (DR 8.5% vs. non-DR 3.8%; HR 2.9, 95% CI: 1.1-7.7, p = 0.03) but not with non-sudden cardiac death (DR 7.7% vs. non-DR 4.6%; HR 1.5, 95% CI: 0.6-3.9, p = 0.5). Interestingly, increased hs-TnT, measured in stable phase of CAD, was also associated with DR (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: DR seems to be associated with cardiac death, and more specifically, with SCD in patients with CAD and type 2 DM. DR might be a novel marker of microvascular cardiac disease resulting in ongoing myocardial injury and SCD.

title: Circulating LRG1 in heart failure: association with type 2 diabetes and antidiabetic therapy class.
authors: Alrosan K, Odeh M, Alqudah A, Abudalo R, Qnais E
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently coexist and share remodelling and inflammatory mechanisms. Although leucine-rich α-2 glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) has been identified as a biomarker associated with vascular remodelling, fibrosis, and inflammation, its role in HF patients with type 2 diabetes and its connection to antidiabetic treatments remains unclear. METHODS: 115 patients with HF were divided into three groups for this cross-sectional study: HF who had no previously documented diagnosis of diabetes mellitus and were not receiving antidiabetic medication at enrolment (n = 42), HF with T2DM treated with DPP-4 inhibitors (n = 35), and HF with T2DM treated with SGLT-2 inhibitors (n = 38). The groups' clinical characteristics, metabolic parameters, and circulating LRG1 levels were compared. RESULTS: LRG1 levels differed significantly across the groups (p = 0.002), with the lowest levels observed in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group. A post hoc analysis revealed a significant difference between the SGLT-2 inhibitor group and group of no previously documented diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (p = 0.001). No significant correlations were observed between LRG1 and clinical or metabolic variables. CONCLUSION: Circulating LRG1 levels in HF patients differed between study groups, with the lowest levels observed in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group. These findings suggest an association between treatment group and LRG1 levels, but the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference regarding the effects of antidiabetic medications on inflammatory and remodelling pathways.

title: Atomically dispersed nanoactivators drive innate mitochondrial biogenesis for active neuroprotection in ischemic stroke.
authors: Liu M, Lin M, Chen M, Huang Q, Xia C, Chen L, Chen Y, Zhang J
abstract: Mitigating mitochondrial bioenergetic failure is a pivotal yet formidable neuroprotective goal in treating cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). However, conventional pharmacological interventions remain largely confined to passive antioxidant defense, which temporarily scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS) without restoring organelle function. Here, we report a bimetallic nanoactivator (RMV) designed to drive active mitochondrial revival for rescuing ischemic tissues. RMV comprises atomically dispersed ruthenium sites anchored within an oxygen-deficient manganese hydroxide matrix via synergistic Ru-O-Mn bridges. Benefiting from its intrinsic mitochondriotropic properties, RMV effectively intercepts aberrant electron leakage and breaks the self-amplifying cycle of ROS-induced ROS release through cascade multi-enzyme mimetic activities. Importantly, transcriptomic profiling and ultrastructural analysis reveal that RMV transcends passive antioxidant defense by functioning as a bioactive switch. It revives the suppressed SIRT1-PGC1α-TFAM signaling axis, fundamentally driving mitochondrial biogenesis and the reconstruction of functionally intact respiratory chains. In a murine stroke model, RMV treatment induces a 1.52-fold expansion of the neuronal mitochondrial biomass under ischemic stress, thereby suppressing neuronal apoptosis, reducing infarct volumes, and favorably reshaping an M2-polarized neuroimmune microenvironment. These integrated effects yield robust and sustained neurofunctional recovery. Our study shifts the neuroprotective paradigm from reactive damage control to active mitochondrial biogenesis, offering an atomically engineered strategy for ischemic stroke management.

title: Platinum-based Nanozyme screening coupled with ISAR-generated pyrophosphate for dual-mode detection of cardiovascular disease-associated miRNA-21.
authors: Chen M, Zhu J, Xu L, Liu W, Qi D
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Early assessment of cardiovascular disease (CVD)-associated molecular alterations may provide valuable information for disease monitoring and clinical evaluation. MicroRNA-21 (miRNA-21) is involved in multiple cardiovascular pathological processes and has been widely investigated as a CVD-associated circulating biomarker. Rationally modulating the activity of platinum-based nanozymes can expand sensing strategies and improve the performance of miRNA-21 detection. Herein, four platinum-based nanozymes are synthesized via a one-step reduction method and systematically evaluate their peroxidase (POD)-like catalytic activities. Among them, the NiPt nanozyme exhibits a favorable apparent peroxidase-like activity under an equal mass concentration, with the lowest Michaelis-Menten constant of 0.462 mM. Then, a colorimetric and fluorescent dual-mode biosensor is developed for the rapid and sensitive detection of miRNA-21 via NiPt nanozyme couple with the target-triggered invading stacking primer-based amplification reaction (ISAR). Sequence-specific hybridization between miRNA-21 and the designed hairpin DNA probe initiates ISAR and generates pyrophosphate (PPi), which suppresses the peroxidase-like activity of NiPt NPs and enables fast, instrument-free, and colorimetric qualitative detection of miRNA-21 at 5 × 10-11 M. Simultaneously, the Cy5 fluorescence signal exhibits sensitive quantitative detection of miRNA-21 with a limit of detection (LOD) of 2.27 × 10-13 M over a linear range of 10-12-10-9 M (R2 = 0.971). The biosensor demonstrated high selectivity toward miRNA-21 against representative interfering miRNA sequences and showed consistency with qRT-PCR in clinical serum samples from heart failure patients and healthy individuals. This dual-mode platform provides a rapid, sensitive, and reliable approach for miRNA-21 detection, demonstrating potential utility for CVD-associated biomarker analysis and further clinical investigation.

Defect-engineered piezoelectric heterointerfaces enable ultrasound-amplified built-in electric fields for bacterial envelope destabilization and implant infection control.
authors: Liu P, Lu S, Chen J, Cheng H, Yan J, Yao X, Wang G, Zhang X
abstract: Built-in electric fields (BIEFs) at piezoelectric heterointerfaces are widely invoked to assist charge separation, but their contribution to antibacterial activity under ultrasound remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a defect-engineered piezoelectric heterointerface strategy to investigate BIEF-related interfacial electrical effects. Density functional theory (DFT)-guided screening identifies a dual-vacancy piezoelectric heterojunction (BTO3-X/MoS2-X) with enhanced interfacial polarization. Under ultrasound, BTO3-X/MoS2-X efficiently kills Staphylococcus aureus, accompanied by pronounced bacterial envelope destabilization. This response is accompanied by membrane lipid perturbation, increased permeability, respiratory inhibition, and intracellular ROS accumulation. GROMACS simulations show that a model lipid bilayer destabilizes only under a sufficiently strong applied electric field. In infected implant models, ultrasound activated BTO3-X/MoS2-X reduces early peri-implant bacterial burden and promotes a repair-favorable inflammatory microenvironment. These findings highlight the potential contribution of BIEF-related interfacial electrical effects to ultrasound responsive antibacterial activity and offer a defect-engineering strategy for implant infection control.

title: From laboratory quantification to rapid on-site testing: Screening of high-affinity monoclonal antibody pairs targeting the RSV F protein and analytical evaluation across multiple assay platforms.
authors: Peng S, Liu Q, Duan C, Liu J, Wang R, Huang Y, Long A, Deng Q
abstract: Monoclonal antibodies against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) F protein are key reagents for antigen-based diagnosis, yet antibody pairs compatible with multiple assay formats remain limited. In this study, BALB/c mice were immunized with recombinant postfusion RSV F protein, yielding six hybridoma cell lines secreting anti-RSV F monoclonal antibodies. The antibodies were characterized by indirect ELISA, Western blotting, and surface plasmon resonance, and the optimal sandwich pair was selected by cross-pairing ELISA. The mAb-14/mAb-26 pair showed high affinity and the best pairing performance and was used to establish double-antibody sandwich ELISA (DAS-ELISA), magnetic microparticle-based chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt nanoparticle-based lateral flow immunoassay (Au@Pt-LFIA). The limits of detection were 0.25, 0.04, and 0.78 ng/mL, respectively. Au@Pt-LFIA achieved an approximately fourfold lower visual detection limit than conventional colloidal gold immunochromatography without additional signal-amplification steps. None of the three methods showed detectable cross-reactivity with the seven tested heterologous respiratory pathogen antigens. In preliminary clinical sample testing, the positive percent agreements of DAS-ELISA, chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt-LFIA were 90.0%, 93.3%, and 83.3%, respectively, and the negative percent agreements were 100.0% for all methods. These results support mAb-14/mAb-26 as a versatile antibody pair for RSV antigen detection across complementary laboratory and on-site assay platforms.

title: Mechanisms underlying the effects of Buyang Huanwu Decoction against sepsis-induced ARDS using network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Tan W, Wang C, Liu X, Deng J, Sang Z, Hu X
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHW), a classic formula from Yilin Gaicuo Qing Dynasty, is indicated for stroke in patients with qi deficiency and blood stasis in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia. In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), the pathogenesis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with qi deficiency, blood stasis, and heat-toxin obstructing the lungs, which align with the therapeutic actions of this formula. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the effects of BYHW on sepsis-induced ARDS and the mechanisms underlying these effects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ARDS was induced through LPS treatment in wild-type and eNOS-deficient (eNOS-/-) mice. The components of BYHW were analyzed using UPLC-UV-MS. Potential associated targets and pathways were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking experiments. Relevant protein and mRNA expression levels were assessed by Western blot analysis, immunofluorescence analysis, or qPCR. RESULTS: BYHW significantly improving the hypothermia, elevated plasma levels of IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6, the lung index and injury induced by LPS in wild-type (WT) mice. However, these effects of BYHW were markedly in eNOS-/- mice. LPS downregulated AQP1 protein expression and upregulated Cav-1 protein expression and the p-P65/P65 ratio in both groups but increased the p-IκB/IκB ratio only in the WT mice. Pretreatment of BYHW increased the expression of eNOS and AQP1, decreased the Cav-1 expression and P65/IκB phosphorylation in WT mice, but the action on the P65/IκB phosphorylation and AQP1 expression were abrogated in eNOS-/- mice. CONCLUSION: BYHW protect against sepsis-induced ARDS may be related to decrease the eNOS-NF-κB-mediated synthesis of inflammatory cytokines and upregulation of AQP1 expression.

A mitochondria-targeting dual-emissive probe for imaging hypoxia-associated biomarkers in early non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
authors: Zhou X, Gu R, Zou Y, Rajalakshmi K, Lee DK, Song JW, Nam YS, Zhu D
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Hypoxia, characterized by a deficiency of oxygen, is associated with the progression of various diseases and the formation of solid tumors. Prolonged hypoxia increases mitochondrial viscosity and induces mitochondrial autophagy, making these important biomarkers of hypoxic conditions. Herein, we developed MI-NO2, a dual-responsive fluorescent probe for the simultaneous detection of nitroreductase (NTR) activity and viscosity. Upon enzymatic reduction by NTR, MI-NO2 is converted to MI, resulting in enhanced intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and a fluorescence turn-on response in the green channel. The sensing mechanism was confirmed by 1H NMR, HR-MS, HPLC, and DFT calculations. In addition, MI-NO2 exhibited enhanced fluorescence in the yellow channel under high-viscosity conditions owing to suppression of the twisted ICT (TICT) process. The probe successfully visualized mitochondrial hypoxia in living cells and distinguished hypoxic from normoxic conditions. Moreover, MI-NO2 enabled monitoring of hypoxia and the associated increase in viscosity increase in an early-stage mouse model of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. Importantly, the probe facilitated the sequential detection of hypoxia-related biomarkers, namely NTR activity and viscosity, using separate fluorescence channels without spectral cross-talk. MI-NO2 therefore provides an imaging platform for the early diagnosis of hypoxia-associated diseases.

title: Hepatic ITGBL1 promotes fibrogenesis and ductular remodeling through integrin-dependent latent TGF-β activation.
authors: He MK, Chen YH, Chen KC, Huang CT, Tang CC, Yang DJ, Lee CH, Hsu CC
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
abstract: Liver fibrosis is a major determinant of chronic liver disease progression and hepatobiliary remodeling. However, extracellular regulators linking fibrogenesis to pathological biliary responses remain incompletely understood. Integrin beta-like protein 1 (ITGBL1) is an extracellular matrix-associated protein implicated in integrin modulation, but its functional role in chronic liver injury remains unclear. A liver-specific doxycycline (DOX)-inducible zebrafish model was established to evaluate the effects of hepatic ITGBL1 gain-of-function in vivo. Fibrogenic and biliary responses were assessed using histologic, molecular, and genetic approaches. Mechanistic studies tested pathway dependence on itgav and ltbp1 using liver-specific genetic ablation, with cilengitide used as a complementary RGD-integrin pharmacologic perturbation. Hepatocyte-specific ITGBL1 induction triggered progressive hepatic stellate cell activation, extracellular matrix accumulation, and chronic fibrotic remodeling. Sustained ITGBL1 expression further promoted ductular reaction and biliary epithelial expansion during chronic liver injury progression. Genetic disruption of itgav or ltbp1 attenuated SMAD3 activation, collagen deposition, fibrogenic transcriptional programs, and associated histological remodeling; cilengitide independently attenuated fibrogenic readouts. These data support a working model in which hepatic ITGBL1 lies upstream of integrin/LTBP1-dependent latent TGF-β/SMAD3 signaling and provide a mechanistic framework for further resolving the molecular interactions among ITGBL1, ITGAV, and LTBP1 and the αv-integrin heterodimer involved. This pathway may represent a therapeutic target for fibrosis-associated biliary remodeling.

Baicalin alleviates renal interstitial fibrosis by targeting SIRT1/HIF-1α signaling pathway.
authors: Zhao S, Zhang Q, Li X, Wang M, Xu A, Zhang J
abstract: UNLABELLED: RENAL INTERSTITIAL FIBROSIS IS A DEFINING FEATURE OF PROGRESSIVE CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE: (CKD) with no effective therapeutic drugs in the clinic. Baicalin (BA) is a natural product sourced from Scutellaria baicalensis and has been proven to treat renal fibrosis and multiple kidney diseases. However, the anti-renal fibrosis effects of BA have not been systematically studied, and its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF STUDY: This study aims to investigate the role of BA in renal interstitial fibrosis and its potential pharmacological mechanism. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The model of unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) mouse and TGF-β-induced cells were employed to evaluate the anti-fibrotic effect of baicalin in vivo and in vitro, respectively. The molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) were used to verify the relationship of BA and its specific target, Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1). The gene-knockdown cells, RNA-sequence analysis, western blotting assay, and RT-qPCR analysis were performed to clarify the BA-SIRT1 interaction and explore its underlying pharmacological mechanisms. RESULTS: BA significantly ameliorated renal fibrosis and promoted renal function in UUO mice, with suppressing fibroblast activation in cultured cells. The results of molecular docking, SPR, and CETSA suggested that SIRT1 is a specific target of BA. The anti-fibrotic effects of BA were abolished after SIRT1 was knocked down. The following RNA sequencing and western blotting analysis revealed that BA inhibits the TGF-β1-induced HIF-α signaling pathway via targeting SIRT1. CONCLUSIONS: This study indicated that BA is a SIRT1 agonist in suppressing the HIF-1α signaling pathway to quell renal fibroblast activation and improve renal function in renal interstitial fibrosis.

title: Targeting macrophage glycolytic-serine metabolism and NF-κB activation by compound Xiancao granule confers renoprotection in diabetic nephropathy.
authors: Zhang S, Chen S, Gan Z, Wang L, Li Q, Huang X, Zhao W, Zhu Y
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Compound Xiancao Granule (FFXCKL), a traditional Zhuang medicinal formula, has long been used for diabetic complications, yet its molecular mechanism against diabetic nephropathy (DN) remains incompletely understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate whether FFXCKL alleviates DN by modulating macrophage glucose-serine metabolism and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses. MATERIALS AND METHODS: db/db mice and high-glucose-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages were treated with FFXCKL. Renal function, histopathology, inflammatory cytokines, macrophage polarization, metabolomic profiles, transcriptomic alterations, and the expression of key glycolytic, serine biosynthetic, and NF-κB signaling molecules were evaluated. Glycolytic (2-deoxy-D-glucose) and serine synthesis inhibitors (NCT-503), together with NF-κB activator and inhibitor (JSH-23), were used to investigate the underlying mechanism. RESULTS: FFXCKL improved hyperglycemia, proteinuria, renal dysfunction, and histopathological injury while reducing fibrosis and systemic inflammation in db/db mice. It suppressed high-glucose-induced M1 macrophage polarization and normalized alterations in glucose and serine metabolism, accompanied by downregulation of HK-2, PKM2, PHGDH, PSAT1, and PSPH. Transcriptomic analysis identified NF-κB signaling as a major pathway affected by FFXCKL, and pharmacological modulation of NF-κB supported its involvement in regulating macrophage inflammatory and metabolic responses. Major limitations include the absence of isotope-tracing metabolic flux analysis and macrophage-specific genetic validation of the proposed mechanism. CONCLUSIONS: FFXCKL attenuated diabetic nephropathy by suppressing macrophage-associated inflammatory responses and improving glucose-serine metabolic disturbances, with effects associated with inhibition of NF-κB signaling. These findings support FFXCKL as a promising multi-target immunometabolic therapeutic strategy for diabetic nephropathy while warranting further mechanistic validation.

title: De novo biosynthesis of meroterpenoid grifolic acid in Yarrowia lipolytica.
authors: Hong Y, Wang J, Wu Z, Lertphadungkit P, Yao R, Zhou B, Bar-Sela G, Cohen I
abstract: Grifolic acid, a potent bioactive meroterpenoid derived from fungi, shows great antitumor and antimicrobial properties. Nevertheless, the difficulty of large-scale chemical production and its minimal presence in natural environments hinder its path toward clinical translation. We developed a de novo grifolic acid biosynthetic route by leveraging the robust metabolic capabilities of the oleaginous yeast Yarrowia lipolytica. By improving the precursor malonyl-CoA supply through ACC1 overexpression and spatially targeting the fungal polyketide synthase ArmB to the vacuolar compartment, we enhanced orsellinic acid accumulation to 8.50 mg/L. We next leveraged AI-guided molecular docking and deep learning kinetic predictions (CataPro and UniKP) to screen candidate enzymes for coupling orsellinic acid with farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP), identifying StbC from Stachybotrys bisbyi as the optimal prenyltransferase for coupling the polyketide with the terpenoid moieties. Integrating the heterologous module with efflux pump engineering (overexpressing native Pleiotropic Drug Resistance ABC transporters) and blocking the competing β-oxidation pathway (through HBD1 deletion) relieved intracellular toxicity and minimized carbon loss. Under optimized conditions using a two-stage glucose-growth and glycerol-supplementation fed-batch regime, the engineered strain produced grifolic acid at 30.5 mg/L in a shaker flask. This work represents the first successful de novo production of grifolic acid in Y. lipolytica, validating a holistic metabolic engineering strategy for the sustainable synthesis of complex meroterpenoids.

title: Modular engineering of aromatic metabolism in Corynebacterium glutamicum enables protocatechuic acid and gallic acid production.
authors: Pei J, Huang Q, Zhang B, Chu X, Wu X, Guo X, Ye B, Zhang B
abstract: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) and gallic acid (GA) are valuable phenolic compounds with diverse pharmacological activities, including antioxidant and antitumor properties, and have broad applications in the food, cosmetic, chemical, and pharmaceutical industries. However, the industrial production of these compounds remains limited by the insufficient performance of current microbial cell factories, resulting in low productivity and high manufacturing costs. Here, an efficient biosynthetic platform based on Corynebacterium glutamicum was systematically established for the production of PCA and GA. Through reconstruction of the PCA biosynthetic pathway, elimination of competing branches in the shikimate pathway, enhancement of the key rate-limiting enzyme, and modulation of the glucose uptake system to increase phosphoenolpyruvate supply, metabolic flux was effectively redirected toward PCA accumulation, resulting in the engineered strain PCA16 achieving a PCA titer of 19.8 g/L in shake-flask fermentation. Building on this platform, GA biosynthesis was established by introducing a mutant pobA from Pseudomonas aeruginosa and further strengthening the shikimate pathway, enabling strain GA06 to produce 7.86 g/L GA in shake-flask fermentation. Upon scale-up in a 5 L bioreactor, GA production was further increased to 25.66 g/L, representing the highest reported titer for GA production using C. glutamicum to date. Overall, this work demonstrates the strong potential of C. glutamicum as a robust microbial chassis for efficient production of PCA and GA, and provides a versatile platform for the biosynthesis of PCA-derived aromatic compounds.
